title: Implement secure staff browser sessions

gates.name: Python typecheck
gates.command: docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend python -m mypy src/face_moment

gates.name: Staff session tests
gates.command: docker compose run --rm backend python -m pytest tests/staff_access/test_sessions.py

verify.summary: Fresh independent T3 verification passed mypy, the focused isolated session test and a separate disposable PostgreSQL/ASGI matrix. It proved exact login/current/logout and cookie behavior, digest-only storage, unchanged absolute expiry, generic invalid-session 401, CSRF 403, normalized-username-plus-IP 429, role projection, secret/digest redaction, cleanup, and linear migration compatibility with TASK-003 staff_users and TASK-006 pipeline_revisions.

Adversarial supported-path verification proved that the configured HTTPS edge does not proxy the accepted root staff-session paths: canonical login/current/login-page requests terminate at Caddy with empty 200 responses, so valid login cannot return 204/cookies and invalid current-session traffic cannot return 401 through the browser-facing boundary.

Attempt 2 fresh independent T3 reassessment passed mypy, the two-test auth/Caddy regression gate, Caddy validation and a fully disposable current-source HTTPS stack. Canonical login/current/logout now cross Caddy with 200/204 behavior, Secure session/CSRF cookies and backend Via; missing and invalid sessions return 401, prior auth/migration/security coverage remains green, and all isolated resources were removed.

Attempt 2 resolved canonical HTTPS path transit, but fresh adversarial proxy-boundary proof found that distinct browser IPs share one login limiter budget because backend keys on the Caddy peer. With limit two, client A received 401,401 and distinct client B's first same-username attempt received 429 instead of an independent 401, violating normalized-username-plus-client-IP semantics and enabling cross-client lockout.

Attempt 3 fresh independent T3 reassessment passed mypy, all three focused auth/migration/Caddy tests, Caddy validation and a fully isolated current-source HTTPS stack. Two distinct clients supplied identical forged XFF yet retained independent username/IP budgets (A 401,401,429; B first 401); canonical session flows, digest-only persistence, absolute expiry, CSRF, invalid-session/rate branches, redaction, Task-003/006 migration compatibility and complete cleanup all passed.

Final Attempt 3 adversarial review confirmed both prior failures resolved: canonical staff paths reach backend without rewrite, and Caddy overwrites forged forwarded identity so distinct origin clients retain separate username/IP budgets while same-client limiting remains enforced. Full T3 cookie, CSRF, expiry, secret-storage, invalid-session, ownership, migration, topology, redaction and cleanup semantics remain intact with no surviving finding or operator question.

The autopilot scheduler closed TASK-004 after correction attempt 3 earned fresh functional PASS and semantic-pass. Two prior semantic failures were durably corrected within the allowed retry budget: canonical HTTPS reachability and originating-client rate-limit isolation.

evidence_required: FT-001-AC-007 RED: valid disposable staff credentials cannot establish and use the canonical absolute-expiry browser session through login/current/logout; GREEN: the same isolated flow satisfies exact cookie and token-hash persistence, expiry, current/logout, generic invalid-session, matching/mismatched CSRF, configured login-rate and redaction branches; decisive comparison: the response/cookie/repository matrix and deterministic rate counts match the contract with no plaintext credential or token marker; artifact: redacted API, repository, CSRF and rate-limit output.
purpose: Provide the HTTPS staff-session prerequisite used by the photographer uploader and later credential revocation.
success_outcome: A provisioned active staff user can log in, read the current principal and log out through secure absolute-expiry browser sessions with CSRF and deterministic login-rate enforcement.
anti_goals: Do not implement password reset/deactivation integration, Photo authorization or uploader endpoints.
Do not add refresh tokens, sliding expiry, session listing, a distributed limiter or a custom error envelope.

forbidden_scope: Inventory business authorization and Photo state
Production credentials or externally reachable internal services
stop_conditions: The accepted cookie, CSRF, role or absolute-expiry contract would need to change.
A plaintext password, session token, CSRF token or token digest would enter URLs or logs.
The work requires a distributed session or rate-limit subsystem.

constraints: staff_access authenticates and returns only staff_user_id, username and role; target capabilities retain business authorization.
Both plaintext tokens contain at least 32 random bytes before URL-safe encoding and only token digests persist.
Login limiting uses normalized username plus IP inside the single-backend pilot.
invariants: Missing, malformed, expired, revoked or inactive-owner sessions return generic 401.
Every unsafe authenticated request requires matching session, CSRF cookie and X-CSRF-Token.
Session expiry is absolute and requests never extend it.
verification_targets: Proof starts in an isolated application instance and disposable PostgreSQL state with one task-unique active staff fixture, no scoped sessions and reset limiter counters; rerun cleanup tears down that instance and removes only task-created session/principal rows before recreating the same known state.
API/repository proof covers login, current principal, logout, cookie attributes, expiry, CSRF, rate limiting and secret redaction.
